name: ADI Global Distribution

THE_CENTRAL_TENSION: the FLOW setup may be the best of the cohort while the ASSET is the one our own prior art already threw out. Both can be true; the court has to price which dominates.

flow_case.why_it_could_be_the_cleanest_forced-sell: our spin doctrine says the US index leg is INVERTED for S&P 500 parents (S&P DJI re-places qualifying spincos same-cycle, making funds forced BUYERS — SOLS/Q/FDXF). The true forced-SELL cohort is (a) SP500 parent -> spinco downgraded to 400/600, or (b) spinco with NO index placement. REZI is an SP600 (small-cap) parent, so a spinco from it is very unlikely to earn any S&P placement — putting ADIG squarely in bucket (b), the strongest forced-sell class.
flow_case.must_verify_before_sizing: S&P DJI's index-announcement PDF for the ADIG treatment. UNKNOWN today and it is the single decisive input — if S&P DOES place it, the flow sign inverts to forced BUYING and the thesis dies.

asset_case_ALREADY_ADVERSE.prior_art_2026-07-04: EXCLUDED — 'the informed-seller trap in the flesh: parent keeps 20%-margin products, spins 6.6%-margin distribution + $1B debt + $900M dividend up'
asset_case_ALREADY_ADVERSE.reading: this is the classic value-destructive spin shape — the parent retains the high-margin business and loads the spinco with debt to pay itself a dividend. Forced selling into a structurally impaired asset is how a flow thesis becomes a permanent loss.

COURT_FRAME_WHEN_IT_SITS: do NOT court this as a quality name — it fails that screen by construction. Court it as a FLOW trade with an explicit asset-quality discount: is the forced supply large enough, and the price low enough, that a structurally impaired distributor is worth renting through the window? Two pre-committed exits are mandatory: a price target tied to flow exhaustion, and a hard time stop at the window's end (~Sept 2), because a flow thesis that needs the business to work has stopped being a flow thesis.
